::: {.lead}
Today you practise three skills that you need every day: you find a fact
on its official website, you keep the part of a screen that matters, and
you check what an AI assistant writes. Each experiment has two parts.
**Part A** is in the app on a computer. **Part B** is on your phone or on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box: a
web address, a name, a number, or yes or no.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a computer with a browser, Word and Excel (or Excel on the
  web at `office.com`), an AI assistant that the university allows (for
  example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your university account), and your
  phone.
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson and in an AI assistant. Do Part B on
  your phone.
- **The prompts:** on the interactive lesson, each prompt has a **Copy
  prompt** button. On paper, type it exactly as it is printed.
- **Never type personal data** (your ID number, phone or address) into an
  AI assistant.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · Find the official source

**The idea:** a **search engine** (Bing, Google) finds web pages. Type 2–4
**keywords**, not a long sentence. Under each result is its **web
address**: it shows whose website it is (`.edu.jo` is a university in
Jordan, `.gov.jo` the government). Open the **official website** of the
owner of the fact. Skip results marked **Ad**, forums and old pages, and
check the year of the page.

**Aim:** find a fact on its official website.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (a web browser)**
:::

1. Search for **Israa University calendar** (`bing.com` or `google.com`).
   Read the web addresses of the first five results, and open the official
   one. Write its web address and the year of its calendar.

   {{< record "The web address … ; the year …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The university's own website: its web address ends in **.edu.jo**. Its
   calendar must be for this academic year (**2026–2027**). Results marked
   **Ad** or **Sponsored** are paid; forums and old pages are not the real
   source.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   It is November 2026. A search shows these results. Which one do you open for the exam dates?

   - [x] www.sunrise-college.edu.jo/calendar · Academic calendar 2026–2027

     Why: .edu.jo is a university website: the college's own page, for this year.

   - [ ] www.sunrise-college.edu.jo/calendar-2023 · Academic calendar 2023–2024

     Why: The website is official, but the page is old: its dates are for 2023–2024.

   - [ ] Ad · www.exam-dates-now.com · Exam dates for all universities

     Why: An ad is paid, and it is not the college's own website.

   - [ ] forum.student-chat.com · Exam dates? Anyone know? (2021)

     Why: A forum shows what people think, and this post is old.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/search-lab.html" poster="sims/search-lab.png" title="Search Lab: which result do you open?" >}}

2. Play **Search Lab**: three searches. Write your score.

   {{< record "My score in Search Lab: … of 3" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   3 of 3 on the first try. The rule: open the website of the owner of the
   fact, skip ads and forums, and check the year.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   You need the price of the Microsoft 365 plan for students. Open it or skip it?

   Open it
   :   www.microsoft.com · Microsoft 365 for students

       Why: Microsoft makes the plan, so its own website has the real price.

   Skip it
   :   Ad · www.cheap-office-keys.com · Office for 2 JD!

       Why: An ad is paid, and a very cheap key is often not legal.

   :   my-tech-blog.net · Office prices (2018)

       Why: A personal blog from 2018: its prices are old.

   :   forum.games-help.com · Is Office free for students?

       Why: A forum shows opinions, not the real price.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A screenshot of the part that matters

**The idea:** a **screenshot** is a picture of the screen, saved as an
image file. In Windows, **Windows + Shift + S** opens the **Snipping
Tool**: drag a box around the part that you need. On an Android phone,
press **Power + Volume down**; on an iPhone, **Side button + Volume up**.
Then **crop** it: keep only the part that matters, cover personal data, and
give the file a good name.

**Aim:** keep only the part of a screen that matters, in a file with a
good name.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Windows and Word)**
:::

1. On the calendar page, press **Windows + Shift + S**, choose
   **Rectangle**, and drag a box around the exam dates. Click the
   notification, then save it (**Ctrl + S**) as `exam-dates.png`.

   {{< record "My file name" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   `exam-dates.png`, or another short name that says what the picture
   shows, in the folder of the course. Windows 11 also keeps a copy in
   **Pictures › Screenshots**.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps of a screenshot in Windows in order.

   1. Press Windows + Shift + S
   2. Choose Rectangle
   3. Drag a box around the dates
   4. Save it with a good name

   Why: First open the tool, then choose its shape, then take the picture, then keep it.
   :::

2. In a new Word document, press **Ctrl + V**. Does the snip appear?

   {{< record "The snip appears in Word (yes / no)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Yes.** Windows + Shift + S puts the snip on the **clipboard**, so
   Ctrl + V pastes it into Word, an e-mail or a chat.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You took a snip with Windows + Shift + S. Where can you paste it with Ctrl + V?

   - [x] in Word, an e-mail or a chat

     Why: The snip is on the clipboard, so any app can paste it.

   - [ ] only in the Snipping Tool

     Why: The clipboard works in every app, not only in the Snipping Tool.

   - [ ] nowhere, it is only a file

     Why: The snip is on the clipboard first; you save it as a file if you need it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On your phone**
:::

3. On your phone, take a screenshot (Android: **Power + Volume down**;
   iPhone: **Side button + Volume up**). Tap the preview, **Crop** it to
   the dates, and save. In which album is it?

   {{< record "The album" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Screenshots**, in Photos or in Gallery.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You took a screenshot on your phone. Where does the phone keep it?

   - [x] in Photos or Gallery, in the album Screenshots

     Why: Phones keep every screenshot in the album Screenshots.

   - [ ] only on the clipboard

     Why: On a phone, a screenshot is saved as a picture at once.

   - [ ] in the folder Downloads

     Why: Downloads keeps files from the Internet, not screenshots.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · An AI draft: check its facts and its number

**The idea:** an **AI assistant** learned from a huge amount of text. It
writes likely words: it is fast for drafts, summaries, ideas, rewrites and
translations, but likely is not always true. It can invent a fact (a
**hallucination**), give old information, or get a number wrong. You check
facts on the official website and numbers in a spreadsheet.

**Aim:** use an AI draft, and check its facts and its number.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and Excel)**
:::

{{< sim file="sims/bill-check.html" poster="sims/bill-check.png" title="Bill Check: is the AI right?" >}}

1. Copy the prompt into the AI assistant. Did the AI add a fact that is
   not in the prompt (a time, a name)?

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write a short notice for the students of our college in three lines. The
   computer lab is closed on Sunday 15 November 2026 for new computers. The
   lecture is in room 105 instead.
   :::

   {{< record "Added facts (or: none)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The notice must keep **Sunday 15 November 2026** and **room 105**. Delete
   every fact that is not in the prompt, for example a time or a teacher's
   name.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   An AI notice says: "The lab is closed on Sunday 15 November 2026. The lecture is in room 105, from 10:00 to 12:00." What do you do?

   - [x] Delete "from 10:00 to 12:00".

     Why: The prompt gave no time: the AI invented it.

   - [ ] Use it as it is.

     Why: The time is not in the prompt, so it may be wrong.

   - [ ] Change the room to 106.

     Why: Room 105 is in the prompt: it is right.
   :::

2. An AI said: "12 pens at 0.25 JD and 5 notebooks at 1.20 JD cost
   **9.50 JD**." Check it in Excel or in **Bill Check**: **=B2\*C2** in
   D2, copy it down, and **=SUM(D2:D3)**.

   {{< record "The total in the sheet" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The sheet: 3.00 + 6.00 = **9.00 JD**, not 9.50 JD. The sheet is right:
   exact numbers belong in a spreadsheet.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="9|9.00|9.0" unit="JD" hint="12 × 0.25, then 5 × 1.20, then add."}
   What is the right total of 12 pens at 0.25 JD and 5 notebooks at 1.20 JD?

   Why: 12 × 0.25 = 3.00 and 5 × 1.20 = 6.00; 3.00 + 6.00 = 9.00 JD.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On your phone** (an AI app, or its website)
:::

3. Send the first prompt again in a new chat. The same words? The same
   day and room?

   {{< record "Same words (yes / no) ; same day and room (yes / no)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The words are usually **not** the same: the AI writes likely words, not
   always the same ones. The day and the room **must** stay the same; if
   they change, the AI made a mistake.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You send the same prompt twice. The two notices have different words, but the same day and room. Is that a problem?

   - [x] No: the words can change, the facts must not.

     Why: An AI writes likely words, so each answer is a little different.

   - [ ] Yes: one of them is wrong.

     Why: Both keep the facts of the prompt, so both can be right.

   - [ ] Yes: the AI is broken.

     Why: A new chat often gives new words: that is normal.
   :::
